articles.title: VICTORY: Meta Strips Facial Recognition Code From Smart Glasses App After Public Outcry
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually yeeted AWS GovCloud credentials to public GitHub because operational security is apparently optional when you're protecting America's cyber infrastructure. The irony is so thick you could mine Bitcoin with it.

articles.title: Iran Signed a Ceasefire — Its Hackers Didn't
articles.summary: Check Point VPN zero-day gave ransomware crews a month-long head start because apparently nobody was watching the watchers. Qilin ransomware affiliate reportedly had a field day with this critical flaw.

articles.title: Meta Blocks NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack, Files Contempt Order
articles.summary: A single character typo in Linux kernel nf_tables code grants instant root access because sometimes the smallest bugs make the biggest holes. Working exploits are now public, so patch your kernels before script kiddies discover copy-paste.

articles.title: AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume: How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload
articles.summary: Critical Check Point VPN flaw bypasses passwords in IKEv1 setups, proving once again that legacy protocols are digital landmines. If you're still running IKEv1 in 2026, this vulnerability is the least of your problems.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers tricked Meta's AI support bot into hijacking Obama's old Instagram account with pro-Iranian messages. When your AI chatbot becomes the weakest link in your security chain, maybe it's time to reconsider that whole 'AI everything' strategy.

articles.title: LiteLLM Flaw CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild, Chains to Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary: NSO Group continues targeting WhatsApp users despite federal court orders because apparently surveillance-for-hire vendors think injunctions are just suggestions. Meta's filing contempt charges, which is like bringing a legal brief to a cyberwar.

articles.title: Cheers to the Winners of EFF’s 18th Annual Cyberlaw Trivia Night!
articles.summary: Meta quietly stripped facial recognition code from smart glasses app after getting caught red-handed by researchers. Nothing says 'privacy-focused' quite like secretly embedding FRT in millions of phones and hoping nobody notices.

articles.title: CBSE retains COEMPT for answer-sheet scanning, shifts data to its own servers
articles.summary: Former IBM exec accuses Big Blue of covering up years of Chinese state hacking because acknowledging breaches might hurt quarterly earnings. William Barlow's whistleblower lawsuit suggests IBM prioritized stock prices over national security disclosures.

articles.title: Securing Your Packagist Account as a Package Developer
articles.summary: Google confirms first AI-discovered zero-day exploit deployed in wild, proving that artificial intelligence is now better at finding vulnerabilities than humans. The same frontier models China desperately wants to copy are revolutionizing both defense and offense.

articles.title: Meta confirms 1000s of Instagram accounts were hacked by abusing its AI chatbot
articles.summary: Cisco SD-WAN zero-day CVE-2026-20245 faces active exploitation with no patch available, because apparently critical infrastructure vulnerabilities wait for no vendor. Limited instances observed, but 'limited' is still too many when it comes to privilege escalation.
